label: radeon-vllm-prefill
platform: vLLM 0.16.1.dev0 on ROCm 7.2.1 (navi, ubuntu22.04, torch 2.9), AMD Radeon Cloud

measurement.method: synthetic code-like filler of N words, asking for a single-word reply, so the measured time is dominated by prefill rather than decode
measurement.transport: Radeon Cloud HTTPS spaces proxy; proxy round-trip is included in every figure
measurement.cold_start_note: the 128-word figure is the first request against a freshly started server and carries warm-up cost, which is why it reads higher than 512 and 2048

finding: Prefill is effectively free up to about 2048 words (0.316s to 0.399s, inside proxy round-trip noise), then costs 2.091s at 8192 words, roughly 5x for a 4x context increase. This is a direct budget for the RAG layer: keeping retrieved context under ~2000 words holds TTFT under half a second, and stuffing 8k words is the single most expensive thing the agent can do to its own latency.
